Let the cube coordinates have \(x=\pm1\) left/right, \(y=\pm1\) front/back, and \(z=\pm1\) bottom/top.

### 1. Examine the given cube

The three marked faces are the top, front, and right faces. They meet at the vertex
\[
O=(1,-1,1).
\]

Their diagonals have endpoints

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Face}&\text{Diagonal endpoints}\\ \hline
\text{Top }(z=1)&(-1,-1,1),\ (1,1,1)\\
\text{Front }(y=-1)&(-1,-1,-1),\ (1,-1,1)\\
\text{Right }(x=1)&(1,1,1),\ (1,-1,-1)
\end{array}
\]

Thus, exactly one of the three diagonals—the front-face diagonal—passes through the common vertex \(O\).

### 2. Fold net D

Label net D as

\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
 & A&B&C\\
 D&E&F
\end{array}
\]

where \(A\) is directly above \(F\). The diagonal-bearing squares are \(B,C,\) and \(D\).

Taking \(F\) as the top face, folding gives

\[
F\to z=+1,\quad
B\to x=+1,\quad
C\to y=-1,\quad
D\to z=-1.
\]

The three marked faces therefore meet at \((1,-1,-1)\). Their folded diagonal endpoints are

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
B&(1,1,-1),\ (1,-1,1)\\
C&(1,-1,-1),\ (-1,-1,1)\\
D&(1,1,-1),\ (-1,-1,-1)
\end{array}
\]

Now rotate the folded cube \(90^\circ\) about the \(y\)-axis using
\[
(x,y,z)\longmapsto(-z,y,x).
\]
This sends:

- face \(B\) to the top,
- face \(C\) to the front,
- face \(D\) to the right,

and their diagonals become exactly the three diagonals on the given cube. This is a rotation, not a reflection.

- **B:** Two marked squares become opposite faces.
- **C:** Two squares fold onto the same face, so it is not a valid cube net.
- **E:** Two marked squares become opposite faces.
